cards.explanation: The answer is that no one can cancel or amend it. Paul says, “Even a human covenant, once it is ratified, cannot be canceled or amended.” Once the ink is dry, it's locked in. That's more than I can say for my New Year's resolutions, which lasted till about lunch.

The answer is Christ. Paul says the Scripture doesn't say “and to seeds…” meaning many, but “and to your seed…” meaning One, “…who is Christ.” He's reading the promise to Abraham one little word at a time, friends. One word, singular, and it points to Christ.

The answer is False. Paul says the law that came 430 years later “…does not revoke the covenant previously established by God, so as to nullify the promise.” The law arrives late, but it doesn't wipe out what came first. Just before this, Paul points out that even a human covenant, once it is ratified, cannot be canceled or amended.

The answer is freely through a promise. Paul says, “…God freely granted it to Abraham through a promise.” He sets that against the law, saying if the inheritance depends on the law, then it no longer depends on a promise. So the promise is the word to hold onto, friends.

The answer is because of wrongdoing. Paul says the law “…was added because of transgressions…” Transgressions are the wrongs people do. He also says it was added until the seed arrives, which tells us it had a set time.

The answer is True. Paul says the law “…was added because of transgressions, until the arrival of the seed to whom the promise referred.” So the law has a limit on it, and the limit is the seed. Earlier, in verse 16, Paul told us the seed is Christ.

The answer is False. Paul asks if the law is opposed to the promises of God, and his answer is, “Certainly not!” Then he gives his reason: “For if a law had been given that could impart life, then righteousness would certainly have come from the law.” So the law and the promises aren't rivals, friends.
The answer is believe. Paul says the promise is given “…by faith in Jesus Christ…” to “…those who believe.” It goes to people who believe, friends. And every one of them gets the same promise.

The answer is so we might be justified by faith. Paul says, “…the law became our guardian to lead us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.” The guardian points toward Christ. And faith is how we're justified.

The answer is False. Paul says, “Now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.” He doesn't leave us still under the guardian, friends. The one doing the leading handed us over to Christ.
The answer is faith in Christ Jesus. Paul says, “You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.” Notice he says all. Everybody comes in the same way, through faith in Christ Jesus.

The answer is True. Paul says, “For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.” Clothed is the picture he uses, friends. And I'm still working on getting my apron to stay clean past ten o'clock.

The answer is False. Paul says, “…for you are all one in Christ Jesus.” Jew and Greek, slave and free, male and female are all one, not separate groups. That's a whole lot of folks fitting in a single batch!

The answers are seed and promise. Paul says, “And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s seed…” Earlier he said the seed is One, who is Christ (Galatians 3:16), so belonging to Christ puts you in that family. Then Paul says you're “…heirs according to the promise.” The promise is what the inheritance goes by, friends, and God gave Abraham that inheritance freely (Galatians 3:18).

The answer is the date set by his father. Paul says the heir “…is subject to guardians and trustees until the date set by his father.” The father picks the date. The heir doesn't get to hurry it along, however many times he checks the calendar.
The answer is His Son. Paul says, “…when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law…” God sent His own Son, friends. And He sent Him when the time had fully come.
The answer is to redeem those under the law. Paul says God sent His Son “…to redeem those under the law…” And the Son was “…born under the law…” Himself. He came to where they were, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says God sent His Son “…to redeem those under the law, that we might receive our adoption as sons.” Adoption as sons is the goal he names, friends. I'll tell you, I know a little something about being picked up and brought home.
The answer is Father. Paul says the Spirit cries out, “Abba, Father!” That's what He calls God, friends. Father, said from right inside our hearts.

The answer is an heir through God. Paul says, “…since you are a son, you are also an heir through God.” Son first, then heir. And Paul has been building toward this since the first verses of the passage, friends.
